After a preposition use -ing; look forward to, used to, object to take -ing.
let, make, see, hear + bare infinitive; the passive of make adds to.
stop, remember, forget, try change meaning with the form.
A participle phrase must match the subject that follows it.
Negative openers (never, hardly, no sooner, not only) force inversion.
So do I / neither can he: invert the helper verb.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Error spotting in divided sentence parts
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: The sentence is split by slashes into four parts; one part holds a grammar fault and the other three are clean.
pyqPatterns.approach: Test the usual suspects in order: verb agreement with the real subject (cover of/as well as phrases), tense after signal words, article by sound, fixed preposition, modal + base verb. The part whose correction you can state is the error.

example.q: The principal, as well as the teachers, / were present / at the annual function / held last Friday.
example.solution: Cover 'as well as the teachers': subject = principal (singular) → 'were present' is the error; it should be **was present**.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Fill in the blank: verb form and tense
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A sentence with one blank where all four options are verb forms (V1/V2/V3, had been, has been, will be).
pyqPatterns.approach: Find the signal word (ago, since, tomorrow, as soon as, before) and decide whether the action is finished, running, or earlier than another action. Read the tense row off the signal, and never put will inside a time or if clause.

example.q: My uncle ___ in Canada since 2019.
example.solution: since + still living → present perfect continuous: **has been living**.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A segment is printed in bold and the options are possible substitutes, often including 'No substitution required'.
pyqPatterns.approach: State the correct form first, then look for it among the options. If the bold segment is already right, choose no substitution — but only after testing agreement, tense sequence and modal + base verb rules.

example.q: If you **would have told** me earlier, I would have helped you.
example.solution: Third conditional if-clause takes had + V3: **had told**.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A full sentence with a trailing comma sits before the blank; the options are auxiliary + pronoun pairs.
pyqPatterns.approach: Copy the sentence's auxiliary, flip the polarity (positive sentence → negative tag), and replace the subject with its pronoun. For special sentences use the fixed tags: Let's → shall we, command → will you, I am → aren't I, nobody → they.

example.q: Nobody called while I was out, ___
example.solution: Nobody → they, and the clause is positive → **did they?**

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Four complete sentences differ in one grammar point each — comparison form, tag, preposition or verb form.
pyqPatterns.approach: Name the point under test and apply its rule to all four: one marker per comparison, than any other inside the group, fixed preposition pairs, no will in the if-clause. The sentence that survives every rule wins.

example.q: (a) Everest is highest peak... (b) Everest is higher than any other peak in the world. (c) Everest is more high... (d) Everest is the most higher...
example.solution: **(b)** — comparative + than any other, exactly one marker.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: The blank follows an adjective, noun or verb (fond, good, angry, insist) or completes a pair begun by no sooner / hardly / not only.
pyqPatterns.approach: Recall the governing word's fixed pair (fond of, good at, angry at a thing) or the correlative's partner (no sooner...than, hardly...when). Reject the preposition that fits the meaning generally but not this word.

example.q: She is not capable ___ handling the project alone.
example.solution: The fixed pair is capable **of** + V-ing.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: The blank sits before a noun whose a/an/the/zero choice is tested — often hour, MLA, university, a superlative, or a school/meals context.
pyqPatterns.approach: Hear the first sound for a/an (an hour, an MLA; a university, a one-rupee coin). Check the the-triggers: second mention, unique things, superlatives, rivers, directions. Zero article with languages, meals and purpose-use nouns like school.

example.q: He waited for ___ hour at the bus stop.
example.solution: 'Hour' begins with a silent h, vowel sound → **an** hour.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: All four options are forms of one family (succeed/success/successful/successfully) and the blank has a fixed slot job.
pyqPatterns.approach: Decide the job the slot needs: after the/of/his → noun; before a noun → adjective; after an action verb → adverb; after a modal → verb. Uncountables (advice, furniture, information) never take -s.

example.q: Hard work is the key to ___.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Either the blank follows a set verb or preposition (avoid, enjoy, look forward to, made him), or the sentence opens with No sooner / Hardly / Never / Not only.
pyqPatterns.approach: Non-finites: preposition or gerund-list verb → V-ing; to-list verbs (promise, decide) → to + V1; make/let/see/hear → bare V1. Inversion: negative opener → auxiliary before subject, with the fixed partner than/when.

example.q: No sooner the bell rang / than the students / rushed out / of the classroom. Find the error.
example.solution: Negative opener needs inversion: 'No sooner **had the bell rung**' — the first part is the error.

solvedExamples.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Neither the coach nor the players ___ happy with the umpire's decision.
solvedExamples.solution: With *neither...nor* the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject. The nearer subject is *the players* (plural), so the verb is plural: **were**. *was, is* and *has been* are singular.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Nearest-noun rule: look only at *players* → plural → **were**.

solvedExamples.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Had he left on time, / he would not miss / the flight / to Chennai.
solvedExamples.solution: *Had he left* is an inverted third conditional (= *If he had left*). The result clause of a third conditional needs **would + have + V3**: *he **would not have missed** the flight*. So segment 2 contains the error.
solvedExamples.shortcut: *Had + V3* at the start → the other clause must be *would have + V3*. Scan only the main clause.

solvedExamples.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Between you and I, / the new manager / does not seem / very competent.
solvedExamples.solution: *Between* is a preposition, so the pronouns after it must be in the objective case: **between you and me**. The rest of the sentence is correct (*does not seem* agrees with *the new manager*).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Cover *you and*: *between I* sounds wrong, *between me* is right.

solvedExamples.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Seldom ___ such a dedicated officer in my career.
solvedExamples.solution: *Seldom* is a negative adverb; when it begins a sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject (inversion). **have I met** is correct. *I have met / I met* lack inversion; *did I met* wrongly uses V3 after *did* (it should be *did I meet*).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Negative opener → question word order → pick the option shaped like a question: *have I met*.

solvedExamples.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The climate of Bengaluru is milder than ___ of Chennai.
solvedExamples.solution: We must compare climate with climate, not climate with a city. The singular noun *climate* is replaced by **that** (plural nouns would take *those*). *it/this* cannot stand for a noun followed by *of* in a comparison.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Singular thing compared → *that of*; plural → *those of*.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The quality of the mangoes sold in these markets ___ improved this year.
practice.solution: The head noun is *quality* (singular); *of the mangoes sold in these markets* is only a descriptive phrase. A singular subject with present perfect needs **has improved**.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The principal, as well as the teachers, / were present / at the annual function / held last Friday.
options: The principal, as well as the teachers,
practice.solution: With *as well as*, the verb agrees with the **first** subject, *The principal* (singular). So it should be **was present**.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My uncle ___ in Pune since 2018.
practice.solution: *since 2018* marks an action that began in the past and continues now, so a perfect (continuous) tense is needed: **has been living**. Simple present, present continuous and past continuous cannot be used with *since* here.
practice.shortcut: since/for → perfect tense; only one option is perfect.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

I will inform you / as soon as the results / will be declared / by the board.
practice.solution: In a time clause introduced by *as soon as*, the simple present is used for future meaning: *as soon as the results **are declared***. *will be declared* is wrong.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

He waited for / a hour at the bus stop / before he finally / took an autorickshaw.
options: a hour at the bus stop
practice.solution: *hour* begins with a silent *h*, so it starts with a vowel sound: **an hour**. *an autorickshaw* is correct.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is not capable ___ handling so much pressure at work.
practice.solution: The fixed collocation is **capable of** + V-ing. *capable for / in / to* are not standard.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Hardly had the guests arrived ___ it started raining.
practice.solution: *Hardly* is paired with **when** (or *before*). *than* belongs with *no sooner*; *then* and *that* are not correlative partners here.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The road is wet and there are puddles everywhere; it ___ rained last night.
practice.solution: The wet road is evidence for a confident conclusion about the past → **must have + V3** (*must have rained*). *should have rained* means it was expected but did not happen; *must rained* and *ought to rained* are ungrammatical.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

If you **would have told** me earlier, I would have helped you.
practice.solution: The main clause *I would have helped* is a third conditional, so the *if*-clause must be past perfect: **If you had told me**. *would* never goes into the *if*-clause.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Gold is more costlier / than silver, / but both are / widely used in jewellery.
practice.solution: *costlier* is already comparative; adding *more* makes a double comparative. Correct: **Gold is costlier** (or *more costly*).

practice.q: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Mount Everest is highest than all other peaks in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any peak in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other peak in the world.
Mount Everest is the higher peak in the world.
practice.solution: Everest is itself a peak in the world, so it must be compared with **any other** peak; dropping *other* illogically compares it with itself. *the higher* is used only between two things; *highest than* mixes a superlative with *than*.

practice.q:
Select the correct question tag.

Nobody called while I was out, ___
practice.solution: *Nobody* makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; indefinite pronouns for people (*nobody, everyone, someone*) are picked up by **they**. The simple past *called* takes *did* → **did they?**
practice.shortcut: Negative word → positive tag; nobody → they.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is looking forward ___ her cousins next month.
practice.solution: In *look forward to*, *to* is a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund: **to meeting**.
practice.shortcut: Test: *looking forward to the trip* works → *to* is a preposition → V-ing.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

No sooner the bell rang / than the students / rushed out / of the classroom.
practice.solution: *No sooner* at the start requires inversion with an auxiliary: **No sooner did the bell ring** (or *No sooner had the bell rung*) *than...*. The rest is correct.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The officer gave us / many useful informations / about the new scheme / and its benefits.
practice.solution: *information* is uncountable: it has no plural and cannot take *many*. Correct: **much useful information** (or *a lot of useful information*).

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She gave me some useful ___ before the interview.
practice.solution: **Advice** is uncountable — no plural -s, no 'an'. 'Advises' is the verb form; the slot needs a noun after 'some useful'.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The furnitures in this room / was bought last year / from a local carpenter / by my uncle.
practice.solution: **Furniture** is uncountable, so 'the furnitures' is the error; once corrected to 'the furniture', the singular verb 'was bought' is right.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  How much ___ does the journey take?
practice.solution: 'Much' goes with an uncountable noun → **time**. 'Hours' is countable and would need 'how many'.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Hard work is the key to ___.
practice.solution: After 'the key to' (here a preposition) we need a noun → **success**. The family: succeed (verb), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb).

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He was praised for his ___ behaviour at the function.
practice.solution: An adjective is needed before the noun 'behaviour' → **courteous**. 'Courtesy' is the noun, 'courteously' the adverb.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The manager spoke ___ to the careless clerk.
practice.solution: 'Spoke' is an action verb, so an adverb is needed → **harshly**. 'Harsh' would describe a thing, not the manner of speaking.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The flowers smell ___.
practice.solution: 'Smell' here is a linking verb (= are when smelled), so it takes an adjective → **sweet**. 'Sweetly' would describe the act of smelling.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He looked ___ when he heard about the accident.
practice.solution: 'Looked' means 'seemed' — a linking verb — so the adjective **sad** describes his state. 'Sadly' would mean he looked in a sad manner.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Between you and ___, the plan will not work.
practice.solution: After the preposition 'between' the object form is needed → **me**. 'I' is only for subject jobs.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The company announced ___ annual results yesterday.
practice.solution: The owner form before a noun is **its**. 'It's' = it is; 'theirs' is a standalone possessive; 'there' shows place.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Rahul and ___ are going to the book fair.
practice.solution: The pronoun is part of the subject of 'are going', so the subject form **I** is needed. Test by dropping Rahul: '*I* am going'.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She ___ to Chennai last year.
practice.solution: 'Last year' is a finished past time signal → simple past **moved**. Present perfect needs a since/for signal; past perfect needs an earlier action.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I have known him ___ 2015.
practice.solution: A point of time (2015) takes **since**; 'for' measures a length (for eight years).

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Look! The cat ___ on the roof again.
practice.solution: 'Look!' signals an action happening now → present continuous **is sitting**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  As soon as the results ___, we will celebrate.
practice.solution: Inside a time clause ('as soon as') the present tense carries future meaning → **are declared**. 'Will' appears only in the main clause.
practice.shortcut: no will after as soon as.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
practice.solution: First conditional: the if-clause takes the simple present → **rains**; 'will be cancelled' stands in the main clause.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I will call you when I ___ home.
practice.solution: The time clause after 'when' takes the simple present for future meaning → **reach**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The patient had died before the doctor ___.
practice.solution: The earlier action (death) already carries 'had died', so the later action takes the simple past → **arrived**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The players ___ the field before the rain started.
practice.solution: Two past actions: leaving happened before the rain started, so the earlier one takes the past perfect → **had left**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  It ___ since morning.
practice.solution: 'Since morning' + still going on → present perfect continuous **has been raining**.
practice.shortcut: since + still running → has been V-ing.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The workers ___ on this bridge for two years now.
practice.solution: 'For two years' measures a duration that continues to the present → present perfect continuous **have been working**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He was exhausted because he ___ for six hours.
practice.solution: The walking continued up to a past moment (was exhausted), so step one tense back → past perfect continuous **had been walking**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The list of candidates ___ been published.
practice.solution: The head noun is **list** (singular); the of-phrase does not change it → has been published.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The bouquet of roses ___ on the table.
practice.solution: Subject = bouquet (singular); roses only describes it → **is**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Every one of the players ___ praised by the coach.
practice.solution: 'Every one' stays singular even with a plural after of → **was**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Each of the girls ___ given a certificate.
practice.solution: Each → always singular → **was**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Neither the manager nor the workers ___ present at the meeting.
practice.solution: With neither...nor the verb follows the nearer subject — **workers** (plural) → were.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Either Ram or his brothers ___ to blame for the loss.
practice.solution: Nearer subject = brothers (plural) → **are**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The committee ___ its decision yesterday.
practice.solution: The committee acts as one unit → singular; the past signal 'yesterday' fixes **announced** (not 'has announced').

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
practice.solution: Subjects ending in -ics (mathematics, physics, economics) take a singular verb → **is**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  More than one student ___ selected for the final round.
practice.solution: 'More than one' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb → **was** — the exam's favourite surprise.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The price of these shoes / are too high / for a student / to afford.
practice.solution: The head noun is **price** (singular), so the error is the plural verb: 'are too high' should be 'is too high'.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He is ___ honest officer.
practice.solution: 'Honest' begins with a silent h — the first sound is 'o' → **an**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She is ___ MLA from Bihar.
practice.solution: MLA is read letter by letter: 'em' — a vowel sound → **an**.
practice.shortcut: an MLA, an M.A., an X-ray.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  My cousin joined ___ university in Delhi last month.
practice.solution: 'University' begins with the consonant sound 'yu' → **a**, whatever the spelling suggests.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  ___ Ganga is considered a holy river.
practice.solution: River names take **the**: the Ganga, the Yamuna, the Nile.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  This is ___ best novel I have ever read.
practice.solution: A superlative (best) always carries **the**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The sun rises in ___ east.
practice.solution: Directions take **the**: the east, the north, the west.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

He goes to **the school** every day.
practice.solution: When 'school' is used for its purpose (studying), no article is used → **goes to school**. 'The school' would mean the building.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

**The man** is mortal.
practice.solution: 'Man' meaning the human race takes no article → **Man is mortal**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Give me ___ time to think; I am almost done.
practice.solution: 'Time' is uncountable, and the speaker needs some (positive sense) → **a little**. Plain 'little' would mean almost none.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He is new in the city and has ___ friends here.
practice.solution: 'Friends' is countable, and being new implies almost none → **few** (negative sense). 'A few' would mean some.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I found ___ one-rupee coin on the pavement.
practice.solution: 'One' begins with the consonant sound 'wu' → **a** one-rupee coin.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The meeting has been fixed ___ Monday morning.
practice.solution: Days and dates take **on**: on Monday, on 15 August.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  We reached the airport ___ 6 o'clock in the evening.
practice.solution: Exact clock times take **at**: at 6 o'clock, at noon.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  My cousin lives ___ Bengaluru.
practice.solution: Large places — cities, states, countries — take **in**; 'at' is for small specific points (at Andheri).

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She is very fond ___ classical music.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is **fond of**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Ravi is very good ___ mathematics.
practice.solution: Skill words take **at**: good at, brilliant at, bad at.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The manager was angry ___ the delay in delivery.
practice.solution: **Angry at** a thing or situation; angry **with** a person. The delay is a thing → at.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The prize money was divided ___ the two winners.
practice.solution: Two parties → **between**; three or more treated as a mass → among.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He has been working in this office ___ five years.
practice.solution: A length of time takes **for**; since needs a starting point (since 2021).

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  No sooner did the bell ring ___ the students rushed out.
practice.solution: The welded pair is **No sooner ... than**; mixing it with 'when' is the classic planted error.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She is not only intelligent ___ hardworking.
practice.solution: The correlative pair is **not only ... but also**, and both parts must join parallel words.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He can ___ three languages fluently.
practice.solution: After a modal the base verb is used → **speak**. No -s, no -ing, no to.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

You should / to consult a doctor / immediately after / the fever returns.
practice.solution: A modal is never followed by to: 'should consult' is correct, so **'to consult a doctor'** carries the error.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  You look exhausted; you ___ have worked all night.
practice.solution: A sure deduction about the past takes **must have** + V3. 'Can have' is not used for deduction; 'should have' would find fault rather than deduce.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  You ___ have taken my permission before using my laptop.
practice.solution: Criticising a past action that did not happen takes **should have** + V3. 'Must have' would only deduce, not find fault.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  If I ___ you, I would apologise at once.
practice.solution: Second conditional (unreal present) uses **were** for every subject: If I were you...

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  If it rains, the match ___ postponed.
practice.solution: First conditional: if + present, main clause **will be** + V3. 'Would' belongs to the second conditional.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  If he had prepared well, he ___ the examination.
practice.solution: Third conditional: had + V3 in the if-clause → **would have** + V3 in the main clause.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  ___ I use your phone for an urgent call?
practice.solution: Formal permission is asked with **May I**. 'Shall I' offers a service; 'should' asks duty.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  When I was young, I ___ play cricket every evening.
practice.solution: A stopped past habit is **used to** + V1. 'Be used to' means 'be accustomed to' and needs -ing after it.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She need not ___ anything about the incident.
practice.solution: 'Need not' behaves like a modal → base verb **say**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  This road is ___ than that one.
practice.solution: Comparative with 'than' → one marker: **narrower**. 'More narrow' doubles the marker.

practice.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Gold is **more costlier** than silver.
practice.solution: 'More costlier' doubles the comparative marker; keep only one → **costlier**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He is the ___ boy in the class.
practice.solution: 'The ... in the class' signals a superlative → **tallest**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Mumbai is larger than ___ city in India.
practice.solution: Mumbai is itself an Indian city, so 'other' excludes it → **any other** city.
practice.shortcut: member of the group → any other.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Kalidasa is greater than ___ poet in Sanskrit literature.
practice.solution: Kalidasa is a Sanskrit poet, so the comparison must exclude him → **any other** poet.

practice.q: Select the correct question tag.  She sings well, ___
practice.solution: 'Sings' needs the auxiliary does; the positive sentence takes a negative tag → **doesn't she?**

practice.q: Select the correct question tag.  They haven't finished the work, ___
practice.solution: Negative sentence → positive tag, copying the auxiliary have → **have they?**

practice.q: Select the correct question tag.  Let's go for a walk, ___
practice.solution: The fixed tag for a Let's suggestion is **shall we?**

practice.q: Select the correct question tag.  Open the window, ___
practice.solution: An imperative takes **will you?** as its tag.

practice.q: Select the correct question tag.  I am late for the class, ___
practice.solution: The fixed tag for 'I am' is **aren't I?** — the one place English drops 'am not'.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He avoided ___ the question directly.
practice.solution: 'Avoid' is on the gerund list → avoid + V-**ing** → answering.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  She is fond of ___ detective novels.
practice.solution: After a preposition (of) the verb takes the gerund → **reading**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  I enjoy ___ to music while working.
practice.solution: 'Enjoy' is on the gerund list → enjoy + V-**ing** → listening.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He promised ___ the assignment by Friday.
practice.solution: 'Promise' takes the to-infinitive → **to finish**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Remember ___ the lights before you leave the office.
practice.solution: A duty still ahead → remember + **to** + V1. 'Remember switching' would recall a past act.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The teacher made the boy ___ the poem aloud.
practice.solution: 'Make' takes object + bare infinitive → **recite**; no 'to' after make in the active voice.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Let him ___ what he thinks is right.
practice.solution: 'Let' also takes the bare infinitive → let him **do**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  No sooner had she seen the snake ___ she fainted.
practice.solution: **No sooner ... than** is a welded pair; 'when' belongs to hardly/scarcely.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.
practice.solution: A negative opener (Never) forces inversion: auxiliary before subject → **have I seen**.

practice.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  Scarcely had he sat down ___ the phone rang.
practice.solution: **Scarcely ... when** is the fixed pair (than pairs with no sooner, not scarcely).
